witnesses.rationale: The exhaustive table always supplies a Word's exact declared arity (scripts/generate-semantics-table.mjs builds one operand per domain position), so no cell can ever be short an operand. Running ADD alone is the whole witness.

The exhaustive table only ever emits well-formed programs (one literal or Word name per domain position, then the Word); a program that fails to tokenize/parse at all is a different axis the table has no domain for. An unclosed vector literal is the simplest witness.

COND has control arity (excluded from the domain table entirely, per scripts/generate-semantics-table.mjs’s arityExclusionReason). A guard that evaluates FALSE with no matching clause and no else exhausts every clause.

DEF's name-position domain representatives (textShort etc.) all happen to already be well-formed symbol lexemes, so the table never exercises a string that tokenizer::is_symbol_token_lexeme rejects. The empty string is not a name.
No domain representative is a reserved Core Word alias, so the table never reaches naming_convention_checker::check_reserved_word_name's refusal. '+' is reserved as an alias of ADD.
BIND's name-position domain representatives are never a live Core or User Word name, so the table never reaches check_bindable_name's Core/User-Word refusal. 'ADD' is a Core Word.
Same gap as nameIsAWord, on DEF's side: no domain representative names a live Core Word, so op_def_inner's core_vocabulary refusal never fires in the table. Redefining ADD is the witness.

Requires two statements sharing state (a live binding, then a DEF of the same name) — the exhaustive table only ever runs one Word against fresh domain literals, so no single cell can set up a binding for a second statement to conflict with.

Requires three statements: define A, define B referencing A, then try to redefine A while B still depends on it. Multi-statement dependency state is outside the one-Word-one-tuple table by construction (Phase 4 pitfall A’s own example).

The exact case Phase 4 pitfall A names: a DEF body that names the very word being defined. The table never writes a word body that references anything but core words and domain literals, so it cannot construct this on its own.

SORT/ORDER's declared nonComparableElement fires only on a structurally non-numeric *element inside* a vector; no chosen domain representative is a vector mixing a numeric-incomparable element (a Boolean) with anything else, so the table's single-domain-per-cell shape never constructs a mixed vector at all.

Same shape of gap as nonComparableElement: JOIN's nonTextElement fires on one bad element inside an otherwise-fine vector, which no single domain representative constructs (the table's vector-domain representatives are homogeneous).

COND has control arity and is excluded from the domain table entirely. A guard clause that evaluates to a non-scalar, non-Boolean value (a String) is neither TRUE/FALSE nor the logical Unknown, so it raises rather than falling through.

MAP's element block runs with control arity of its own — the table's domain tuples only ever supply MAP's own two declared operands (a vector and a block), never a block whose *body* violates the ( x -- x ) contract MAP requires of it, since the block bodies the table writes are never anything but its own placeholder-free structure.

OR-NIL has control arity (it reads the following source unit, not a stack operand) and is excluded from the domain table entirely. A NIL subject with no following unit to fall back on is the declared condition itself.

structureError now means exactly one thing (docs/dev/auditable-kernel-work-order-2026-09.md Phase 1): a failure no Word has declared a condition for yet. DEL's dependents-conflict raise site (execute_del.rs) is exactly that — deliberately left generic in Phase 1 because DEL's contract has no definitionConflict counterpart to DEF's identical check, a words.json gap rather than a wiring bug. It needs two prior statements (define A, define B referencing A) to construct the conflict, so the one-Word table cannot reach it.

The table always runs under the native CLI's default step budget (12,180,000 — docs/dev/mcp-host-profiles.md), which no single-Word cell can plausibly exhaust. --step-limit is the one ceiling the CLI lets a caller shrink directly, so a 4-step program under a 1-step budget reaches it cheaply.

MAX_USER_WORD_DEPTH is 256 nested User-Word activations (interpreter_core.rs); DEF's acyclicity check (LANG.DICTIONARY.ACYCLIC) rules out a word calling itself, so the only way to reach this ceiling is a chain of distinct words each calling the next. That needs 257 DEF statements plus a call — far outside what any single-Word domain cell constructs.

max_numeric_literal_digits (4,096, identical on every host profile per docs/dev/mcp-host-profiles.md) is a property of one literal's own text, which none of the table's domain representatives are long enough to cross — a 4,097-digit literal is the cheapest possible witness and needs no profile override.

Requires a Tier 2 (PI) comparison operand, which is not one of the table's 11 domain representatives (Phase 2 pitfall B: adding a 12th PI domain would multiply the whole table's cell count and its generation cost for one reason alone). Two independently-constructed computable reals with identical enclosures never separate within the comparison budget, so PI PI EQ starves deterministically — no hand-computed digits required (rust/src/interpreter/tier2_undecidable_conformance_tests.rs already pins this exact program).
